hypothesis: Replacing GCC's long-lived broadcast nibble tables with phase-local loads, while simplifying one- and two-source tail transforms, will remove hot YMM table spills and improve complete transform encoding by at least five percent.

variants.name: phase_local_reload
implementation: A production-skew-only noinline T=4 kernel reloaded each nibble-table pair from the immutable FF8 table at the phase that consumed it.
K=3 and K=4 retained prepared tables in registers; K>=5 used phase-local broadcasts.
Two-source tails formed d=x1+x0 and f=x0+a*d, then used [(1+c)*f, (1+c)*d, f, d].
Production skew detection preserved the general synthetic-skew KAT fallback.

static.classification: No coefficient-table vector was spilled. Remaining references were input-pointer prologue stores, transformed-data spills, or cold stack-check bookkeeping.

variants.name: per_product_compiler_barrier
variants.implementation: Compiler-only atomic signal fences bounded every fixed multiplication so broadcasts could not migrate across products; outer phase barriers were removed.

static.conclusion: The extra compiler barriers did not remove a single remaining vector stack reference and slightly enlarged every K>=5 kernel. Across specialized R=4 cells the measured ratios ranged from 0.9806x to 1.0311x, with no confidence interval meeting the 1.05 promotion threshold.

variants.name: packed_lane_tables
variants.reason: AVX2 VPSHUFB is lane-local. Packing low and high nibble tables into opposite 128-bit lanes still requires two shuffles per 256-bit data vector plus cross-lane duplication and recombination. Packing two coefficients has the same lane-extraction cost because transform consumers differ. It saves table-register liveness but adds permutation pressure on the same transform hot path. Since the zero-table-spill implementation changed full encode by only about one percent, the extra permutations cannot plausibly clear the five-percent whole-codec gate on this Zen 5 host.

method.benchmark: Three independent ABBA rounds; 15 retained benchmark iterations; reuse 256; one thread; CPU 10 pinned; SMT sibling 26 reserved; Student-t 95% confidence intervals over round log contrasts.
method.isolation: Both campaigns recorded zero sibling non-idle jiffies, zero contaminated invocation rejections, and no affinity restore errors.
method.correctness: leopard2_backend_ops, leopard2_auto_encode_backend, and the independent leopard2_direct_encode oracle passed. The direct suite covers every specialized K, R=3/4, aligned and ragged vector tails, and unaligned buffers. Every benchmark invocation independently checked direct-versus-transform parity.

conclusion: GCC table spills are visually severe but are not a five-percent whole-encode bottleneck for this T=4 AVX2 kernel. Removing them reduced function bodies by roughly 3-4x yet produced only noise-level runtime changes while adding about 9 KiB of backend text and substantial production-only specialization. No implementation was retained.
